_doc: 5c-2 2c NPC mood (design V1.5 + M7, 2026-11-03). Numbers are START values to tune in dev play. Scores -100..+100. final = clamp(rest + day + clamp(events, -events_cap, +events_cap)).

rest._doc: Townsfolk resting point from a stable hash of the AI id; leaning pleasant (the owner 2026-10-30).

personas._doc: Named NPCs (persona_key): resting point + habit (Codex 2c idea 3, the owner 2026-11-03). Habit lines are about the NPC only - never handing anything to the player.

weary: [pours herself a cup from the battered iron teapot, slowly]
[rests a hand on the iron teapot's lid a moment]
[nudges the iron teapot nearer the coals, unhurried]
glum: [turns the battered iron teapot round on the counter, not looking up]
[lifts the iron teapot's lid, frowns at it, sets it back]

day._doc: Per NPC per Central date (never the epoch). 1 in 6 off, 1 in 6 bright (the owner 2026-11-03, 2c-2); off/bright split by *_mix, each kind's (cheer, energy) push in shape, plus half the ordinary jitter. Ordinary days jitter each axis +-jitter. short-tempered kept the rarest off kind (Codex F7: may be tiresome).

gift._doc: NPC-wide, any giver; needs pt on the row (M7.3). One gift ~+10, any number <= saturate.

busy._doc: Distinct visitors today (Central), cumulative for the day - 'a long day'.

greet_percent._doc: The one greeting-gossip draw (moved from the shard, M7.6). 2b holds still come first.

action._doc: At most one bracketed action per reply; chance per eligible reply; once per conversation and once per NPC per npc_gap_s.

causes._doc: A cause is only an event moving the deciding axis by >= min_points; gift_helped when a gift lifts cheer >= helped_min on a low day (Codex idea 1).

_clause_echo_doc: Integrated trial 2026-11-03: skip the cause clause when the reply already says its gist (one regex per clause family).
_place_doc: Where the mood half of the voice line goes: head = conversation-wide head beside the dials cue (gentler, cache-friendly); turn = beside each turn (M3b: stronger). Re-measured 2026-11-03 per the owner (M10).

risky_patterns._doc: the owner 2026-11-03 (M9 answer 1): scenery is fine; these invented claims are not - illness, stock shortage, slow service / busy excuse, other people. Handled like excuse_patterns: retry, then the sentence goes. Tuned on the 318 integrated-trial replies: tone ('I'm busy enough',) is left alone - it is mood, not an invented fact. 2026-11-04 (26b-a4b tuning, narrowed after Codex r2 F5): + the NPC's OWN work excuses ('I've crates to unpack', not), OWN aches (not), debts (not 'I don't owe money'). Step B 2026-11-08 (Codex Step B r1 finding 3: the illness words matched anywhere - healer answers, denials and were cut; the owner, chat, 2026-11-08 on natures): illness now = the NPC saying it is ill NOW, or an ache/illness given as the reason it cannot serve. Long-standing aches and family/apprentice/sweetheart mentions are an approved exception (nature flavour), so own-ache and patterns are dropped; invented incidents (a thief broke in), stock, delays and debts stay caught. Step B r2 (Codex Step B r2 findings 1-2): the ache-as-excuse check needs the NPC's own body part and an actual refusal ('I'm too ill to'), not any illness word before 'won't' (a healer's 'If you are ill, I won't turn you away' passes); a remedy is not an illness; and a service delay or refusal is caught on its own ('we're closed', 'can't help you today') so cutting an illness sentence can't leave a bare refusal behind - nothing usable left -> the neutral fallback.
illness: \b(?:I'?m|I am|I feel|I'?m feeling|I am feeling|I'?ve been|I have been)\s+(?:(?:a (?:bit|little|touch)|rather|quite|so|very|awful(?:ly)?|terribly)\s+)?(?:sick|ill|unwell|poorly|feverish|under the weather)\b

\b(?:I'?ve|I have|I'?ve got|I have got|I'?ve caught|I caught|I'?ve a|I have a)\s+(?:a\s+)?(?:fever|cough|chill|head\s?ache|stomach\s?ache|tooth\s?ache|belly\s?ache|the (?:sniffles|cough|fever|flux|pox))\b(?!\s+(?:remed\w*|cure\w*|draught|tonic|potion|tea|salve|medicine|herbs?|poultice|syrup|mixture|elixir|for (?:you|it|that|this)))

\b(keep|kept) you waiting\b|\bbe a while\b|\b(behind|backed up) (on|with)\b|\btoo busy\b

\b(?:I'?ve|I have|I've got|I have got|there'?s|there are|we'?ve got)\b[^.!?]{0,30}?\b(?:crates|sacks|grain|flour|stock|goods|orders|barrels|boxes|chores|work|a list|a long list|much|plenty|deliveries|bales)\b[^.!?]{0,25}?\bto (?:unpack|mend|move|weigh|stack|haul|shift|count|sort|finish|get through|be moved|be done|be unpacked|be counted|be stacked)\b(?![^.!?]{0,15}\b(?:for you|your)\b)

_tuning_2026_11_08: Step B dev play test (the owner, chat, 2026-11-08): every NPC was content (edge 30 -> content 68% of NPC-hours in the band sim). bands.edge 30 -> 15 and day.jitter 10 -> 15: content ~38%, ~45%, plain ~17% (sim, 600 NPCs x 28 days x 24 h); the 1 in 6 off / 1 in 6 bright days unchanged. style.content may be a list (one per NPC per day); how_angles = one angle per ask, so ten NPCs do not all reach for the sunshine. The weather angle was tried and dropped (variety trial 2026-11-08: NPCs invented weather that contradicted each other - rain coming vs the sun out).
how_angles: Say it through your work or craft.
Say it through something in front of you - a tool, your goods, the room.
Say it in one short plain line.
Say it through a small comfort of the day - a meal, a warm drink, a tune you hum.
Say it with a turn of phrase from your trade.

style._doc: M11 trial (the owner 2026-11-03): a speaking-style hint per band, used by voice when voice_style is true. Tone only - no reasons, no excuses, no stage actions. 2026-11-04: lively reworded - read as curt on gemma4:26b-a4b (10/48 judged short-tempered). Round 2: dropped - it read cheerful and warmed strangers (22 judge votes vs 4).
style.weary: Speak like someone worn out: fewer, slower words, a little flat, perhaps a pause.
style.glum: Speak like someone low in spirits: quiet and flat, little enthusiasm, no exclamations.
style.short-tempered: Speak curtly: clipped, impatient, straight to the point.
style.cheerful: Speak warmly and brightly: friendly and pleased, perhaps a light joke.
style.lively: Speak with energy and pace: quick, bouncy words, keen to get things moving - full of beans, never curt or impatient.
content: Speak in your ordinary, even way: plain and practical.
Speak in your ordinary way, with a dry touch of humour.
Speak in your ordinary way: easy and unhurried, glad to talk about your trade.
Speak in your ordinary way: polite and a little reserved.
